sections.h2: What should you know before selling a house in Daytona Beach, FL?
sections.html:
Daytona Beach sits in Volusia County, so the property appraiser, tax collector and clerk are county offices, while permits, rental registration and code enforcement come from the city. Knowing which office holds which record saves most of the running around.

The city is known for its beach, its speedway and its colleges. A seller's best route depends on the house: a well-kept home near the beach can list, while a rental, an inherited property or a house needing heavy repairs often suits a direct as-is purchase.

  • List with an agent when the house shows well and you can wait for a lender-financed buyer.
  • Sell privately when you are comfortable handling contracts and disclosures.
  • Take a cash purchase when speed, condition or tenants are the obstacle.

sections.h2: How did Daytona Beach become what it is today?
sections.html:
Daytona Beach was founded in 1870 and incorporated in 1876, and its name is credited to founder Matthias D. Day of Mansfield, Ohio. In 1926 the separate towns of Daytona, Daytona Beach and Seabreeze merged under the Daytona Beach name.

The hard-packed sand made the beach a testing ground for high-speed cars in the early 1900s, and by the 1920s it carried the label of the World's Most Famous Beach. Daytona International Speedway, built by NASCAR founder William France, has hosted the Daytona 500 since 1959. The city notes that driving and parking on the beach is still allowed, which is rare.

Education is part of the picture as well. The city counts six institutions of higher learning within its limits.

sections.h2: Do Daytona Beach landlords have to register their rental?
sections.html:
Yes. In 2024 the City Commission repealed the old Residential License Program and replaced it with a rental registration rule that covers owners of fewer than five units. Registration is annual and applies to long-term rentals, defined as at least six months plus one day.

An owner can request a voluntary inspection, and once the property passes, the registration fee is waived for the following year. Anyone planning to rent for less than six months plus one day should call the city's Business Tax Office at (386) 671-8140 to learn whether the zoning allows short-term rentals. The Rental Property Program office is at 125 S. Palmetto Ave.

If you are selling a rental, make sure the registration is current. A buyer or title agent may ask for it.

sections.h2: When are Volusia County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Volusia County bills in early November and collects without penalty through March 31. The county tax collector's page lists the discount schedule and the delinquency rules.

  • Bills are mailed on or about November 1.
  • Discounts: 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January, 1 percent in February and none in March.
  • March 31 is the last day to pay without penalty and the deadline for a tax deferral application.
  • Taxes become delinquent April 1, and a 3 percent minimum charge is added.
  • April 30 is the deadline for new installment-plan applications.

Unpaid accounts are advertised and then included in the annual tax certificate sale. A certificate becomes a first lien on the property and can be the basis for a tax deed application after two years, so a seller who is behind should settle the balance at or before closing.

Exemptions follow the state calendar: applications go to the county property appraiser by March 1 of the tax year, and a homestead exemption can total up to $50,000 in assessed value reduction.

sections.h2: What do permits and code issues mean for a Daytona Beach sale?
sections.html:
Any unfinished permit or open code case can surface in a buyer's due diligence. The city's Code Compliance team identifies blighted or substandard housing and works toward its repair or removal.

Before you list, pull the permit history on the address. If you replaced a roof, added a room or changed electrical or plumbing without a final sign-off, resolve it first. If you are selling a house in poor condition to a cash buyer, the buyer will take the issues with the property, but the title company still needs to see that liens and open cases are paid or accounted for.

Ask the city about unpaid code charges when you request payoff figures. Those amounts can attach to the parcel and appear in a title search.

sections.h2: What does the deed transfer cost in Volusia County?
sections.html:
Florida charges documentary stamp tax of 70 cents per $100 of consideration on a deed, and Volusia County follows that standard rate. Miami-Dade is the exception.

The Department of Revenue states that every party to the document is liable, so the purchase contract and the closing statement decide who actually pays. The tax goes to the county clerk when the deed is recorded.

The clerk also charges recording fees under section 28.24: $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 per additional page, plus trust fund and technology charges. Warranty, special warranty, quitclaim and trustee's deeds are all taxable, and a deed that transfers title also triggers a reassessment of the property to just value on the following January 1.

sections.h2: How do foreclosure, probate and eviction rules affect a Daytona Beach sale?
sections.html:
Florida law sets the clocks, and they influence how long you have to sell.

In a judicial foreclosure, the sale is held between 20 and 35 days after the final judgment unless the plaintiff agrees to a longer period. The winning bidder posts a deposit of 5 percent, and objections are due within 10 days of the certificate of sale.

For an inherited home, the court process comes first. Summary administration is available when the non-exempt estate does not exceed $150,000 or the person died more than two years ago. Creditor claims are barred after the later of three months from first publication of the notice or 30 days after service.

For a tenant, three days' written notice applies to nonpayment, and the sheriff posts 24 hours' notice before carrying out a writ. If you are selling with a lease in place, ask the buyer in writing whether they will honor it.

faqs.q: Is rental registration required in Daytona Beach?
faqs.a: Yes, for owners of fewer than five residential units under the 2024 ordinance. Annual fees are $75 per unit after the first year, and a voluntary inspection that passes waives the next year's fee.

faqs.q: When are Volusia County taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. A 3 percent minimum charge is added then, and unpaid accounts are advertised after April 30 and can move to the annual tax certificate sale.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Daytona Beach house with an unregistered rental?
faqs.a: You can, but fix the registration first. A title agent or buyer may ask for proof of compliance.

faqs.q: How much is the deed tax on a Daytona Beach sale?
faqs.a: The rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration under section 201.02, paid to the county clerk when the deed is recorded. The sale contract decides which side covers it.

faqs.q: Do I lose my homestead protection when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. The Save Our Homes cap ends on a change of ownership, and the buyer starts at just value the following January 1. Ask the Volusia County Property Appraiser about portability if you are moving to another Florida homestead.
